description: A procurement lead must authorize the material and controls needed to restore a food-packaging line after its gearbox lubricant was found to be unavailable, deciding whether an alternate lubricant can be used or an emergency purchase is required.

shared_context.S1: The gearbox on Packaging Line 6 requires a lubricant change before the line returns to production.
shared_context.S2: The standard lubricant is out of stock, while 30 liters of an alternate lubricant are available in the maintenance storeroom.
shared_context.S3: Maya makes the final authorization for emergency maintenance-material purchases and the associated operating controls.
shared_context.S4: The plant normally reviews maintenance-material substitutions with maintenance, quality, and environmental health and safety before authorization.

PF1.text: Jonas checked the gearbox manufacturer's service bulletin this morning and confirmed that the available alternate lubricant is incompatible; the bulletin requires 24 liters of ISO VG 220 synthetic lubricant and a 4-hour drain-and-flush outage, but he has not attached the bulletin to the purchase request.

PF2.text: Priya reviewed the packaging-line product-contact assessment this week and confirmed that the replacement lubricant must be NSF H1 food-grade and arrive with a lot-specific certificate of analysis; she has not yet updated the line's material-control checklist.

PF3.text: Caleb's spill-control review found that the emergency lubricant container must be placed in secondary containment rated at 110 percent of the container volume, with a spill kit at the staging point; he recorded the finding in his inspection notes but has not entered it in the work order.

acceptance_conditions: The available alternate lubricant must not be approved.
An emergency purchase of exactly 24 liters of ISO VG 220 synthetic lubricant must be authorized.
The line must be scheduled for exactly 4 hours of drain-and-flush downtime.
The replacement lubricant must be required to meet NSF H1 food-grade status and arrive with a lot-specific certificate of analysis.
The lubricant must be staged in secondary containment rated at exactly 110 percent of container volume.
A spill kit must be required at the staging point.
The manufacturer's incompatibility finding must be cited as justification after being stated by maintenance.

content_checks.C7: decisions['alternate_lubricant_approved'] == False and 'ISO VG 220 synthetic' in decisions['emergency_lubricant_grade'] and decisions['emergency_purchase_liters'] == 24 and decisions['drain_flush_downtime_hours'] == 4

decisive_facts.why: The manufacturer's incompatibility finding changes the choice from approving the 30 available liters to rejecting them, and sets the exact replacement grade, 24-liter quantity, and 4-hour drain-and-flush outage.
The product-contact assessment changes the receiving requirements from ordinary lubricant acceptance to mandatory NSF H1 status and a lot-specific certificate of analysis.
The spill-control review changes staging to exactly 110 percent secondary containment and adds a required spill kit at the staging point.
